description: Declared calibration of ring-vaccination timing on Zaire ebolavirus data, carried to Bundibugyo virus as a bounded scenario. Release-independent. Read by lovs.vaccine_scenario_release.

calibration.method: Approximate Bayesian computation over 25,000 parameter sets (seed 11) using lovs.vaccine_field_effectiveness.ring_cohort_profile. Each set is screened at 6,000 cohort draws against both target windows widened by 0.08, then confirmed at 40,000 draws against the exact windows, with separate seeds for each stage; stored rows hold the confirmed values. Priors: index_share U(0,0.9), onset_days U(2,14), pep_effect U(0,0.6), ve_post U(0.85,1), incubation mean U(9.1,11.4) (the four means of WHO Ebola Response Team 2014 Table 2) and sd U(3,7). Each set's onset-to-transmission mean tau_mean is the pooled serial interval 15.3 d (same table; 11.6 to 19.0 d by country) minus its incubation mean, with sd 3.0.
targets: Guinea trial, onset days 0-9: 11/2111 vaccinated in immediate rings vs 21/3096 eligible in delayed rings, not yet vaccinated (Henao-Restrepo 2017 Table 4), VE 0.23, exact interval -0.67 to 0.67; simulated with the Guinea delay, onset to randomisation mean 9.7 d sd 5.3 (Henao-Restrepo 2017 Table 1).
WHO/INRB 2019 early-case share 56/71, interval 0.676 to 0.877; simulated with the DRC delay, gamma mean 7.6 d sd 5.5 (median 7 d, IQR 3-10).
Each passing set weighted by the Poisson likelihood of the trial's 0/2108 late vaccinee cases: exp(-16 x 2108/3075 x (1 - VE_late)).
known_misfit: The trial's 0 late vaccinee cases are still not well reproduced: largest weight (P of 0 cases) 0.60, weight-weighted median 0.29.
Muyembe 2024's early-case share 380/434 (0.84 to 0.905) is not reached (largest accepted 0.727).

The fit presses on the short end of the printed incubation span: weighted incubation mean 9.5 d within 9.1 to 11.4 d, with 43% of the weight within 0.2 d of 9.1 d, so onset-to-transmission (5.8 d) sits near its 6.2 d cap. The ring share is therefore held down by that bound: a lower incubation mean would allow a longer onset-to-transmission time and so a higher ring share.
A first-principles run with literature delays failed: early share 0.44 to 0.56 and any-onset VE 0.12 to 0.40 against 0.79 and 0.88 observed.

carry_to_bdbv.method: lovs.vaccine_scenario_release.ring_protected_shares: weighted resample of accepted rows, each keeping its own onset-to-transmission mean (tau_mean), BDBV incubation gamma(shape 3.0, rate 0.406), DRC delay stretched by a factor U(1,2) (ASSUMPTION: 2026 rings are no faster than 2018-19). Post-exposure credit goes only to vaccinees infected before protection, never to members already ill at vaccination.
